added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: the opening a compacted tier is re-compacted from is never consulted: for a counter the run has not yet carried in, the bucket's opening takes the row's own reading, and _counter_reading of a compacted row is its closing counter, so a higher tier built from minute rows opens its first window one sample late. Measured with one job's counter running 0, 1000, 1000, 2000 inside one hour of one boot: compact_rows(raw, 'hour') gives {open 0, close 2000}, advance 2000, while compacting those minute rows to hour gives {open 1000, close 2000}, advance 1000, the minute rows themselves being right ({open 0, close 1000} and {open 1000, close 2000}). The plan names this assertion explicitly ('compacting raw to minute to hour agrees with compacting raw straight to hour') and no test in the node covers it; the equality held at the base revision only vacuously, neither side carrying an opening at all.

the equality test is named for a comparison it does not make: index.ingest is handed the raw rows (line 124) and TelemetryIndex.partitioned_total is therefore measured over the raw rows, while the compacted rows are totalled by this file's own helper _compacted_run_total (line 51), which re-derives the figure in Python from the shared predicate. The query layer never reads a compacted file in the test, so the manifest's and the landing fragment's claim that the run-partitioned total over the compacted rows equals the partitioned total over the raw rows they replace rests on a re-derivation rather than on either instrument that will read the record; measured directly, the index over the compacted rows returns runs=0 and total None for the restart window (raw: 520,000) and 200 for a two-window run (raw: 300).

a compacted row's opening counter is read by nothing in the query layer: partitioned_total selects measurement rows for the counter's own name, while a compacted row stores its closing under that name and its opening under a separate measurement name (open.<name>), so a window answered from a compacted tier alone still under-reports -- runs=0 and total None across a restart where the raw rows give 520,000, and 200 where the raw rows give 300 over two windows. The base revision reads the same way, so the node introduced nothing here, but the row that would close the gap now exists and no reader consults it.

the manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm, so the added-failure count this review would derive from them is unmeasured (the read path annotates it from those two fields) and the promotion suite-delta check has no arm to compare; the gate log it does record was taken at revision 41ef8974 with a dirty tree (two modified modules and one untracked test file), so no gate log on disk belongs to the committed revision -- I re-ran the named gate against the committed blobs and it is green (87 passed, guard 1 passed, ruff exit 0).

the landing fragment installs the equality unconditionally -- the run-partitioned total over the compacted rows equals the partitioned total over the raw rows they replace, 520,000 over the restart window -- with no caveat that the hour tier built from minute rows does not reproduce it and that the 520,000 is the compacted rows' own figure rather than the query layer's answer over those rows; a reader of the landed record is told a deletion licence that has been demonstrated for one tier only.

follow_ons: the query layer does not read a compacted row's own open block, so a window answered from a compacted tier still under-reports (measured: runs=0 and total None across a restart where the raw rows give 520,000; 200 against the raw rows' 300 over two windows); teaching partitioned_total the opening, or which tier the caller actually asked for, is its own node, and the base revision reads the same way, so it is a pre-existing gap the change neither closed nor widened

the tier-chain equality the plan asks to be asserted (raw to minute to hour against raw straight to hour) needs its own test beside a repair in _compact_run, where a bucket's opening must come from the first contributing row's own open block rather than from its closing reading

the reviewed run's manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm, so its added-failure count is unmeasured here and the promotion suite-delta check will find no arms to compare; the separately dispatched test node's arms would close both, per the reviewed node's own gate sentence

the reviewed node's dispatch says its done-when names no artifact, while its fence lists the landing fragment path and its landing contract asks for the fragment; it wrote the fragment (correctly shaped as a bare section, unlike the sibling node's) and the stale sentence belongs to whoever owns the dispatch template
